Frank A. Capell published The Strange Death of Marilyn Monroe in 1964 as a Herald of Freedom pamphlet, two years after the actress was found dead. Capell, publisher of the Herald of Freedom, questioned the official ruling that her death was a simple overdose.

The pamphlet examines the chloral hydrate evidence and Monroe's financial troubles, arguing that the accepted story leaves too much unexplained. It helped launch a long line of books claiming her death was arranged rather than accidental. Read today, it is an early piece of the Monroe conspiracy literature that has never gone away.
